message.content:
Tina chooses 2 distinct numbers from \(\{1,2,3,4,5\}\). There are

\[
\binom{5}{2}=10
\]

possible pairs, and Sergio has \(10\) choices, so there are \(10\cdot 10=100\) equally likely outcomes.

List the possible sums of Tina’s two numbers and count how many Sergio choices are larger:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{Tina's pair} & \text{Sum} & \#\{s\in\{1,\dots,10\}:s>\text{sum}\}\\
\hline
(1,2)&3&7\\
(1,3)&4&6\\
(1,4)&5&5\\
(1,5)&6&4\\
(2,3)&5&5\\
(2,4)&6&4\\
(2,5)&7&3\\
(3,4)&7&3\\
(3,5)&8&2\\
(4,5)&9&1
\end{array}
\]

Total favorable outcomes:

\[
7+6+5+4+5+4+3+3+2+1=40
\]

Thus the probability is

\[
\frac{40}{100}=\frac{2}{5}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{2}{5}}\).
